subject: Tiered per-token parity + escape path — proposal for Nimbus
messages:
From: Ellie Carter <ellie.carter@nimbus.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing alignment request — parity with OpenAI for evaluation

Laura,

Thanks for the demo today — the latency profile and observability looked solid. We have one outstanding gating item from our finance and platform teams: cost. Our CFO asked whether Redwood can match per-token parity to our current OpenAI rates for the first 12 months while we run a pilot and validate latency/quality.

Specifically:
- Target: parity on text-generation per-token rates for up to 500M tokens/month (pilot tranche).
- We'd also like clarity on commit tiers (monthly commit vs annualized) and any clawback/escape language if we scale beyond the pilot.

Can you send a concrete packaging option (pricing + minimal legal/escape language) we can show procurement this week?

Thanks,
Ellie Carter
Director, Platform Engineering — Nimbus Inc

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing alignment request — parity with OpenAI for evaluation

Ben / Vivek — forwarding Ellie from Nimbus. They want per-token parity vs OpenAI for a 12-month pilot up to ~500M tokens/month. Procurement will push for permanent parity unless we set clear constraints. Attaching the pricing model draft (pricing-model-v2.xlsx) and an MAP (mutual-action-plan.docx).

Quick ask: what is the maximum leeway we can give on per-token for Hosted API while protecting unit economics and keeping the option to route/upgrade to Dedicated if they grow? My suggested levers below — please comment inline quickly so I can respond to Ellie today.

Suggested levers:
- Time-limited parity: match OpenAI per-token for 6–12 months for the first 500M tokens/mo, then revert to standard Redwood tiers unless they convert to a committed slab.
- Commit tiers: three tiers (Baseline 0–200M, Growth 200–1B, Scale 1B+) with step discounts; a higher committed discount for 12-month prepay vs monthly commit.
- Escape path: include a defined "escape credit" (one-time onboarding credit) and the option to move to Dedicated with a migration credit applied to first month.
- Usage policing: streaming / tool-calling and fine-tuned endpoints priced at a premium to prevent loss-leading high-cost workloads.

Ben — what can we offer on a one-time onboarding credit? Vivek — any restrictions from leadership on parity vs OpenAI when it threatens margin?

—Laura
Product Sales, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing alignment request — parity with OpenAI for evaluation

Laura — see inline proposal.

High-level approach (concise):
- Tiered time-limited parity: match OpenAI per-token for the pilot period (6 months recommended, up to 12 months if they commit to a MAP that includes Quarterly business reviews). Parity only applies to base text-generation tokens (no fine-tune, no multimodal, no embeddings).
- Guardrails: parity capped at 500M tokens/month. Overage above that billed at our standard post-pilot tiered rates unless they sign a committed slab.
- Commit slab conversion: allow conversion of pilot consumption into a 12-month committed slab with retroactive application of a conversion credit equal to 25% of pilot spend (applied once at conversion).
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a $25k one-time setup credit applied to the first invoice; if they go to Dedicated within 180 days, treat that credit as a migration credit toward the first month.
- Legal/escape language: simple clause — parity provided for pilot term; Redwood reserves the right to adjust for material cost changes and to exclude non-standard workloads.

Risks to call out when you write the external reply:
- If they bundle high-cost streaming or fine-tuned inference under parity we lose margin quickly.
- Engaging Dedicated too early without clear throughput profile could leave us exposed on committed infra.

If you want, I can draft the email to Ellie and attach the two docs. Approve the 6 vs 12 month tension (I recommend 6 + optional 6 extension conditional on MAP).

-Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Ellie Carter <ellie.carter@nimbus.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing alignment request — parity with OpenAI for evaluation

Ellie — thanks again for the clear ask and for walking us through your token profile. Per internal review we can offer the following simple, time-boxed package to make the evaluation economics comparable to your current OpenAI spend while protecting both sides.

Proposal (summary):
- Pilot parity: Redwood will match OpenAI per-token rates for base text-generation tokens for a 6-month pilot (option to extend a second 6-month tranche if quarterly business reviews show parity is meeting quality/latency goals). Parity applies up to 500M tokens/month.
- Scope exclusions: parity excludes embeddings, fine-tuning, multimodal/vision, and any custom kernel/edge routing costs. Streaming call overhead (long-lived connections) will be billed at +10% on top of per-token to account for connection costs.
- Overage and conversion: any usage above 500M tokens/month billed at standard Redwood post-pilot tiered rates. If Nimbus elects to convert to a 12-month committed slab within the pilot, they receive a conversion credit equal to 25% of pilot spend applied once at conversion.
- Onboarding/migration credit: one-time $25,000 credit to apply against the first invoice. If Nimbus transitions to Dedicated within 180 days, we will re-apply that credit as a migration credit to the first Dedicated invoice.
- Governance & escape language (short): parity provided only for the pilot term; Redwood may suspend parity for specific workloads that materially deviate from the agreed token profile or are demonstrably loss-leading. Any long-term parity requires an explicit committed slab agreement.

Attachments: pricing-model-v2.xlsx (breakdown by tier, example invoices), mutual-action-plan.docx (dates, pilot milestones, success criteria).

Next steps:
1) If this sounds workable, can procurement confirm they have the docs they need? We can sign a 1–2 page pilot addendum this week.
2) Schedule a 30-minute kickoff (we'll bring product + infra) to pin SLOs and traffic shape.

Ben is cc'd and has approved the outline; Vivek is looped for final leadership visibility. Happy to tweak scope (e.g., reduce to 3-month pilot or raise the parity cap) if procurement needs stronger risk controls.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
